topics.summary: A server owns its listening descriptor. Each accepted peer owns its descriptor, decoder, output buffer, offset, and deadline. A database store owns its SQLite connection. A prepared statement owns its statement handle. A transaction owns rollback responsibility until commit succeeds. The gateway owns its dispatcher thread, and the thread owns its separate database connection.

topics.title: B.5 Queue and Metrics Ownership

reading.title: B.6 Database Interface and Implementation
paragraphs: The store interface makes submission outcomes explicit: accepted, duplicate, conflict, or full. Completion is a separate operation. The worker’s apply method combines duplicate recognition and effect recording in one transaction. File-backed tests verify reopen and concurrent-connection behavior.

The implementation deliberately has a small schema and no connection pool. It requests WAL and full synchronous behavior, configures a bounded busy timeout, and rejects a newer unsupported schema version. It does not manage replica failover, online schema migration, receipt pruning, or encrypted storage.

Notice the exception boundaries. A failed connection setup releases the handle. A statement releases its compiled representation. A transaction that has not committed attempts rollback during destruction without throwing from that destructor. The outer application translates failures into bounded protocol outcomes or startup errors.

The gateway’s two connections have different execution owners. They share a file but not unsynchronized transaction objects. This design keeps local concurrency understandable while relying on SQLite for the database’s actual transaction serialization.

topics.title: B.9 Gateway Process
topics.summary: The gateway creates persistent intent before replying accepted. Its dispatcher repeatedly selects pending work, uses stable request identity, validates worker responses, and records completion. Random seeding is performed during main-thread startup so a seeding failure is handled before the background thread begins.

blocks.text:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(HarborDispatch VERSION 1.0.0 LANGUAGES CXX)
include(CTest)
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
find_package(SQLite3 REQUIRED)
find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter REQUIRED)
option(HARBOR_SANITIZERS "Enable AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer" OFF)
add_library(harbor_options INTERFACE)
target_compile_features(harbor_options INTERFACE cxx_std_20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
  target_compile_options(harbor_options INTERFACE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
  if(HARBOR_SANITIZERS)
    target_compile_options(harbor_options INTERFACE -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
    target_link_options(harbor_options INTERFACE -fsanitize=address,undefined)
  endif()
endif()
add_library(harbor_core INTERFACE)
target_include_directories(harbor_core INTERFACE $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>)
target_link_libraries(harbor_core INTERFACE harbor_options Threads::Threads)
add_library(harbor_store src/store.cpp)
target_link_libraries(harbor_store PUBLIC harbor_core SQLite::SQLite3)
if(NOT CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
  message(FATAL_ERROR "The executable transport lab targets Linux; pure headers can be ported separately.")
endif()
add_library(harbor_net src/net.cpp)
target_link_libraries(harbor_net PUBLIC harbor_core)
foreach(app worker gateway client)
  add_executable(harbor_${app} src/${app}.cpp)

reading.title: B.10 Client and Build Graph
paragraphs: The client is a protocol tool, not a full business SDK. It prints the response and reports transport failure separately. A script must interpret application outcomes explicitly. It does not retry automatically or generate job identities, which keeps ambiguous-outcome policy visible to the caller.

The CMake graph declares the actual dependencies and test targets. The default build requires installed SQLite development support, Python for integration tests, and Linux for native transport. It does not fetch remote third-party source during configuration.
